title: A Phase 1/2 Study of DIAG723 in Adults with Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT)
official: A Phase 1/2, First-in-Human, Multicenter, Ascending Single-Dose and Multi-Dose Study to Assess the Safety of DIAG723, a Novel Bispecific ALK-1 and BMPRII Agonist Antibody in Adult Patients with Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (DIAMOND trial)
summary: Main objective: To assess the safety and tolerability of DIAG723 following subcutaneous administration as single ascending doses (Part A) and multiple-dose regimens (Parts B and C) in adult patients with Hereditary Haemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT).
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male or female participants aged ≥18 years at the time of consent.
2. A confirmed diagnosis of Hereditary Haemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT) based on Curacao criteria or genetic testing.
3. Adequate hepatic and renal function as defined in the protocol.
4. For Parts B and C: Participants with moderate-to-severe HHT, including those with a history of recurrent epistaxis and/or anemia requiring medical management.
5. For Part C: Participants with HHT and confirmed pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) as defined in the protocol.
6. Ability and willingness to comply with all study procedures and requirements.
7. Provision of written informed consent prior to any study-specific procedures.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of any clinically significant uncontrolled medical condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would interfere with participation in the study or interpretation of results
2. Any condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, makes the participant unsuitable for inclusion in the study.
3. History of recent thromboembolic events or significant cardiovascular disease.
4. Active or recent clinically significant infection, including but not limited to hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV, or tuberculosis.
5. Use of anti-angiogenic therapies or other prohibited concomitant medications as defined in the protocol.
6. Recent nasal ablative procedures or interventions that could interfere with assessment of epistaxis.
7. Known hypersensitivity to monoclonal antibodies or any component of the investigational medicinal product.
8. Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
9. Participation in another investigational study or receipt of an investigational medicinal product within the timeframe defined in the protocol.
10. Prior exposure to DIAG723 (applicable for Part C).
